claim: Port 0x6B (zxnDMA mode) transfers exactly the programmed length; port 0x0B (Zilog mode, since core 3.1.2) transfers length + 1 bytes as the Z80 DMA chip does, so code ported from a Z80 DMA is one byte out on 0x6B.
limit: Measured on a KS1 (core 3.03.00, nxsuite D03): length 16 moved 16 bytes on $6B, 17 on $0B; length 0 moved 1 byte on both. Before core 3.1.2 the mode was chosen by NextREG 0x06 bit 6, since removed.

evidence.text: DMA page, read 2026-11-23: zxnDMA mode moves exactly the programmed byte count; Zilog mode moves length + 1; since core 3.1.2 the port number selects the mode.
evidence.quote: In zxn-DMA mode, the transfer length is exactly the number of bytes programmed.

evidence.text: KS1 Issue 2, core 3.03.00 (nxsuite D03): length 16 moved 16 bytes on port $6B and 17 on $0B; length 1 moved 1 / 2; length 0 moved 1 on both.
